problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{2}^{x}-4?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={2}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/2fe0fb3f0f5d302d39f6ad578148c4973618595452b59fea8a8bb2399ef92ddc.png)

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{2}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/98c622f4675812dcada993e4022398aac18f37cda76bbaf3ecbe6147c6e5bc97.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $4$ units down to give $y=-{2}^{x}-4.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,-5)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/c5d06a922bc2fc4841bc33d0bd7dcc68244ce5ebacfd717aaa710044ec5c3caa.png)
